transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in today because... people have actually started pointing out how I've been moving lately. Sometimes it's like I'm moving underwater. It'll take me forever just to answer a question or even just get up out of a chair. 

And then other times, I'm doing the exact opposite. I'll just be pacing around my apartment, rubbing my hands together... kind of like I'm trying to shake off a bad call from work. It's just getting really noticeable, so I figured I should come see someone about it.
Have you ever had periods in your life where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or wired, to the point where you didn't need much sleep for several days at a time?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, I don't think I've ever felt unusually energetic or wired like you're saying. I usually need my sleep, so staying up for days without it... no, that doesn't sound like me at all. I've never really had a time where I was just talking a mile a minute or feeling super energized.
Do you ever hear sounds or voices that other people around you cannot hear?

Yeah, I actually do. Um... sometimes I'll hear my old work headset beep. Or I'll hear a voice, kind of sounding like a supervisor, saying my name or telling me I'm "too slow." But the thing is, my laptop will be completely closed, and there's no phone ringing anywhere.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, solve problems, or keep track of your daily tasks recently?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues with that. I mean, I can still focus fine when I need to. I keep track of my daily stuff—like paying bills or doing my chores—without much of a problem. So, no, my memory and my ability to figure things out seem pretty normal to me.
Have you ever been diagnosed with a medical condition, such as a head injury, epilepsy, or a thyroid problem, or have you recently started or stopped any medications or substances?

No, I haven't. I've never had a head injury or seizures or anything like that. And my thyroid is fine, as far as I know. I haven't started taking any new medications either, and I don't really use any other substances. So, no, nothing like that.
When you feel like you are moving underwater, do you ever find yourself getting stuck in a position and staying that way for a long time, even if it is uncomfortable?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I feel really sluggish and heavy sometimes, like I said, but I don't get stuck like a statue or anything. I can still move when I need to, it just takes a lot of effort. But no, I don't hold uncomfortable poses or just freeze up for a long time.
Do you believe that your supervisor is actually trying to communicate with you through these sounds, or do you recognize that these voices are likely not real?

I know they're not real. I mean, my supervisor isn't actually in my apartment. But it's just... I'll hear the old headset beep, or I'll hear this voice that sounds exactly like a supervisor saying my name, or telling me I'm 'too slow.' And this happens when my laptop is completely closed and there's no phone ringing anywhere. So I know it's not actually happening, but it sounds so real when I hear it.
Even though you know the voices aren't real, do you ever feel like there is some kind of hidden meaning or a specific message directed at you behind those sounds?

Well, I don't know about hidden messages in the sounds, but... I do get these thoughts sometimes. Like, even when my mood is better and I'm having an okay week, I get completely convinced that the ticketing software from my old job is tracking me. Like it's somehow following me through different job sites and flagging me as an unreliable employee. It feels really real to me, even if it sounds strange to say out loud.
How long have you been convinced that the ticketing software is tracking you and flagging you as an unreliable employee?

Um, it's been a while. Both the voices and that whole thing with the tracking software... I'd say they've been around for about a year and eight months now. And it's not just happening when I'm in the worst of my sadness, either. It's there even when my mood is mostly fine and I'm having a decent week.
Are there any other beliefs or ideas you hold that others might find difficult to believe or that you feel strongly about, besides the idea that the software is tracking you?
No, not really. It's just the stuff with the software and the voices I mentioned. I don't really have any other strange ideas or beliefs like that. Just the tracking thing.
